claims.claim: Structurally related esaxerenone, a lipophilic methyl-carboxamido-aryl heterocycle with a para-substituted anilide and a trifluoromethyl/trifluoromethoxy aryl group, has absolute oral bioavailability of 89.0% fasted and 90.8% fed in healthy subjects.
Nilotinib, a lipophilic heteroaryl amide with trifluoromethyl, has an assumed absolute oral bioavailability of 31% under fasted conditions in humans, still above the 20% threshold.

All other L1 gold-context records report oral bioavailability values of 31-100% or qualitative good bioavailability (isradipine 37%, elinzanetant 36.7%, glasdegib 77%, encainide 76-78%, meloxicam 91%, tolfenamic acid 91-100%, MK-8628 good); no L1 record reports F <20%.

The low physicochemical prior (logD 5.82, unfavorable solubility) is an uncertain prior and is not affirmative evidence for F<20%; transferable positive measurements from structurally related lipophilic amides support F>=20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule.
No L2 records are available at this level; only L1 gold-context records.
No experimental solubility, permeability, or first-pass data for the query; the low prior is physicochemical only.
Some L1 values were measured in cirrhosis/hepatic disease populations and may not fully transfer to a no-condition setting.
Nilotinib F is an assumed value and MK-8628 is qualitative, so they provide weaker quantitative anchors.
No formulation, dose, or food-effect data for the query.
content.decision_summary: All L1 gold-context records are affirmative for F>=20%, with measured values from 31% to ~100% and qualitative 'good' bioavailability; structurally related lipophilic amide analogs (esaxerenone 89-91%, nilotinib 31%) support F>=20%. The low physicochemical prior is not affirmative evidence for F<20% and is outweighed by transferable positive measurements. Prediction: high, moderate confidence.
